Vascular atlas

Three-dimensional visualizations of the heart, neck and brain vasculature. Every scene draws on the SPL Head & Neck Atlas, the JHU parcellation and BrainCharter data; the space is RAS, in mm. The info boxes note that the scan is cut at z ≈ −160 mm and that the JHU alignment is approximate (scale 0.865, rotation 3.6°, median residual 1.2 mm).

Delay investigated in the context of vessels

The blood arrival delays painted onto the vessel trees themselves, at two spatial resolutions.

Arteries and veins coloured by blood arrival delayResolution: JHU atlasdelay_and_vessels↗

The BrainCharter arterial and venous trees painted with the group-average rapidtide delay of the JHU territories: each arterial point takes the delay of the territory it lies in, each vein the mean over the territories it drains. Arteries, veins or both, the delay-territory map as an overlay, hover for vessel names, click to trace a vessel back to its source.

Arteries and veins coloured by voxel-level blood arrival delayResolution: voxel leveldelay_vessels_voxel_resolution↗

The same vessel trees carried to the voxel level: instead of one delay per JHU territory, each arterial and venous point takes the voxel-level rs-fMRI delay measured where it lies, so the delay gradient can be followed along the vessels themselves. Arteries and veins side by side, rotating together; arteries, veins or both.

Gradient delay vector field derived from the isochrone movie

The gradient of the delay field around the vessels: the vein case as arrows, and the artery + vein case as flow lines rebuilt from the isochrone movies.

Delay gradient arrows around the veinsCase: veinsgradient_field_vein↗

The group-mean lagtime field sampled as arrows beside the vein trees: each arrow is the delay gradient (∂t/∂x, ∂t/∂y, ∂t/∂z, central differences at 2 mm) at a point 3 or 6 mm from a vessel, in the plane perpendicular to it, coloured by whether it points into the vessel, away from it or along it. If veins collect late blood, arrows beside them should point into the vein; the panel tallies the in/out fractions per vein group, with significance from the ridge test (spin and shift nulls).

3dtry.github.io/gradient_field_vein/gradient_arrows_veins.html

Arteries and veins side by side, rotating together, with a moving-front wave, colour by delay gradient versus blood-flow direction, and the spin-null test on the cosine between the two fields.

What do we know from theory regarding gradient flow?

Poiseuille flow: where does the delay change?Case: theoryfluid_dyn↗

Laminar flow in a straight vessel with the parabolic Poiseuille profile: blood entering at z = 0 reaches a point (z, r) at t = z / v(r), so the arrival-time gradient has an axial part (∂t/∂z = 1/v(r), constant along the vessel) and a radial part (∂t/∂r grows with z and steepens toward the wall). Arrows show both components and their resultant, the slice disc shows t(r) as concentric equal-delay rings — the delay changes across the vessel, not around it — and a radial-mixing slider blunts the profile toward a plug, where the radial gradient vanishes.

3dtry.github.io/fluid_dyn/poiseuille_delay_gradient_theory.html

Visualize Clustering in 3D

The 30 JHU territories as nodes in 3D, clustered by their delay correlations and compared against the arterial and venous trees.

Delay-correlation clusters × arterial vs venous treesCase: JHU L1 territoriesvlustering_visualisation↗

The 30 JHU L1 territories as nodes in 3D, joined by delay-correlation edges (r ≥ 0.70) and coloured by arterial root, venous outlet or Ward clusters of the delay data: does the anterior/posterior block structure of the delay-correlation clustering match the arterial supply partition (ICA L / ICA R / basilar), the venous drainage partition (torcular / sigmoid L / sigmoid R), or just spatial proximity? Trees grow from their roots and Ward merges play as animation, territories explode apart, and ARI, Mantel and spin-null tests quantify the agreement. Drop a 4036×30 territory-delay matrix or a 30×30 correlation matrix (.npy or CSV, JHU L1 column order) — computed in the browser, nothing is uploaded.

3dtry.github.io/vlustering_visualisation/delay_clusters_vs_trees.html

Improved Version: comparison of 2 clustering methodsCase: JHU L1 territoriesclustering_2Methods↗

The same 30 JHU L1 territories as nodes in 3D, now comparing two clustering methods side by side: Ward on the correlation-derived distance d = √(2(1 − r)) versus Ward on the correlation matrix R as a data matrix (rows as 30-dimensional feature vectors, Euclidean distance), next to the arterial supply partition (ICA L / ICA R / basilar). ARI, Mantel and spin-null tests quantify how well each method's anterior/posterior block structure matches the arterial supply. Drop a 4036×30 territory-delay matrix or a 30×30 correlation matrix (.npy or CSV, JHU L1 column order) — computed in the browser, nothing is uploaded.

3dtry.github.io/clustering_2Methods/delay_clusters_two_methods.html

Three panels: reference in the middle, our method on the right, alternative on the leftCase: JHU L1 territoriesclusters_ourmethod_reference_alternative↗

The 30 JHU L1 territories as nodes in 3D, shown in three side-by-side panels. The middle panel is the fixed arterial-root reference partition (BrainCharter tree, ICA L / ICA R / basilar — it never changes with k or data); the right panel is our method (Ward on the correlation matrix treated as a data matrix: rows as 30-dimensional feature vectors, Euclidean distance) and the left panel the alternative (Ward on the correlation-derived distance d = √(2(1 − r))). Both Ward clusterings are recomputed when k changes, spheres stay at their territory centroids in all three, trees grow from their roots and Ward merges play as animation, territories explode apart, and ARI, Mantel and spin-null tests quantify the agreement with the arterial supply and venous drainage partitions. Drop a 4036×30 territory-delay matrix or a 30×30 correlation matrix (.npy or CSV, JHU L1 column order) — computed in the browser, nothing is uploaded.
